newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto loyalist allowed into ousted PM's house.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto loyalist allowed into ousted PM's house.

text.p: Troops guarding the residence of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto in Islamabad on Tuesday allowed past the chief minister of Pakistan's North West Frontier Province to visit his ousted leader.

Aftab Sherpao was the first Bhutto loyalist known to have gained access to the prime minister's house since President Farooq Leghari issued a proclamation dismissing her in the early hours of Tuesday.
Sherpao earlier visited Leghari, who also dismissed dissolved the National Assembly and appointed a caretaker premier to oversee snap elections.

"What has happened has been a big shock for her," Sherpao told reporters before driving through a gateway into Bhutto's residence in his official vehicle. "We have been fighting against it and now it has happened," he said of her dismissal.
Sherpao said Bhutto, 43, was unlikely to take the removal of her three-year-old government meekly.
"She is a fighter. She has faced worse situations," he said.
Former government ministers who tried to visit her earlier in the day said they were turned back by police.
